documents.s: Decide whether to connect tenants or consolidate them

documents.t: Organizations frequently face the challenge of integrating multiple Microsoft 365 tenants after mergers, acquisitions, divestitures, regional compliance requirements, or operating model changes. There are two primary approaches: Cross-Tenant Synchronization Full Tenant Migration Selecting the wrong strategy can create significant operational, security, compliance, and user experience challenges. This document proposes a decision framework for planning Microsoft 365 tenant integration.
Examples: Subsidiary acquisition Business integration Organizational restructuring
Examples: GDPR German BDSG Local Data Residency
Examples: HQ and Regional Tenant Shared Services Model Multi-Tenant Governance
Decision FrameworkBusiness requirement to architecture path Option 1

Cross-tenant synchronization provisions B2B collaboration users and supported security groups into a target tenant. It is a one-way provisioning process; source identities remain responsible for authentication. It does not migrate mailboxes, files or Teams content. See the supported objects and group limitations. For same-cloud user synchronization, each synchronized user needs Entra ID P1 in the source tenant. Group synchronization and cross-cloud synchronization require Entra ID Governance or Entra Suite. Target-tenant features can have their own licenses. Devices and contacts are not supported sync objects. See the current license and object table. Only internal member users in the source tenant can be synchronized; source external users and internal guests are excluded. Synchronization can match an existing target B2B user, but it cannot merge that identity with a target internal account. See source user types and existing-user matching. Group synchronization creates static security groups in the target, including when the source is a Microsoft 365 group or dynamic security group. It does not recreate a Microsoft 365 group's mailbox or Team, and nested groups are unsupported. Use Sync only assigned users and groups, not Sync all users, for group synchronization. A target-only sign-in block can be undone when a later source-user change is synchronized. Do not rely on that block as a durable cross-tenant access restriction. Review the source account, synchronization scope and cross-tenant access policy together; removing a user from sync scope soft-deletes the target user. See target changes and synchronization scope. Users remain in their original tenant. Workload content remains in its original tenant; selected identity attributes are provisioned into the target tenant. Role-assignable group synchronization is supported when role-enabled group sync is available in your environment. In the target tenant, enable both inbound group synchronization and inbound role-enabled group synchronization. In the source tenant, map isAssignableToRole directly, only during object creation, before adding these groups to scope. This copies role-assignability, not role assignments; assign target-tenant roles separately. The property cannot be changed after creation, and adding the mapping does not convert previously synchronized non-role-assignable groups. See the current group synchronization conditions. Group support also depends on the cloud pair: same-cloud commercial and US Government synchronization support users and groups; same-cloud 21Vianet and the documented cross-cloud pairs support users only. Do not apply the group scenario to every cloud combination. See supported cloud pairs.
Cross-Tenant SynchronizationIdentity connection while data remains separated
No mailbox migration. No SharePoint migration. No Teams migration.
There is no mailbox or file cutover, but provisioning, access-policy and collaboration changes can still disrupt users. Estimate risk from the actual design and pilot results.
A limited identity pilot may be quicker than a content migration, but duration depends on object count, attribute mapping, access policy, testing and approvals. Estimate the schedule after discovery.
Synchronization does not move workload content, but user attributes are provisioned into the target tenant. Review those data flows and cross-tenant access separately.
Mailboxes stay in source tenant. SharePoint remains separate. Teams remains separate.
Multiple tenant context. Potential collaboration complexity.
Multiple tenants remain. Multiple governance models remain.

Scenario Recommendation Separate workload storage Consider synchronization when content should remain in existing tenants; assess identity-attribute transfers separately Regional requirements Validate data location, access and applicable requirements; synchronization alone establishes no compliance outcome Regional Autonomy Strong Fit Temporary Integration Strong Fit M&A Due Diligence Phase Strong Fit Option 2
Users and workloads are migrated into a target tenant. Decommission source services only after retained data, identity dependencies, billing and migration exceptions have been resolved.
Full Tenant MigrationWorkloads move into one operating tenant

The following items are discovery categories, not a promise that one tool transfers every object, permission or sharing link. Record supported items, exclusions and required recreation for each selected workload migration method.

A consolidated tenant can simplify data discovery and administration. Copilot readiness still depends on permissions, licensing, data quality and policy; consolidation is not a prerequisite.

Mailbox remains in source tenant. Users collaborate through B2B relationship.
Mailbox moved to target tenant. Single mailbox strategy.
Separate content repositories. Separate search indexes. Separate permissions.
Unified content repository. Unified governance. Configure and test Copilot access against target permissions, licensing and policy.

Some resource-tenant operations still require a tenant context. Multi-tenant organization experiences can improve cross-tenant people discovery and collaboration, but synchronization does not merge workload data or every Teams experience.
Validate target Teams access, recreated resources and retained migration exceptions.

Benefits: Validate access to target organizational data Test search results after indexing Apply and test target security policies Review migrated knowledge and remaining source dependencies

Cross-tenant synchronization can preserve separate workload storage and administration. It still provisions identity attributes across tenants and enables cross-tenant access. Determine permitted data flows, storage locations and responsibilities with the organization's privacy and legal owners before enabling it; neither synchronization nor tenant separation by itself establishes GDPR compliance. Microsoft describes these responsibilities.

Long-term integration is required. Unified governance is required. The approved Copilot operating model calls for consolidated accounts and workloads. Centralized security is required.

documents.s: Move less data and create a better collaboration model

documents.t: File server migration moves legacy shared folders into modern collaboration platforms such as SharePoint, OneDrive or Azure Files. Assess copy fidelity and service interruption alongside unmanaged folders, stale permissions and unclear ownership. Rank those risks using the source inventory and pilot results.
파일 서버의 자료를 SharePoint나 OneDrive로 옮기기 전에 확인할 항목을 정리했습니다. 파일 소유자와 공유 권한을 정리하고 대상 저장 위치를 정합니다. 시험 이전에서 파일 수, 접근 권한과 사용자 업무를 확인한 뒤 전환하세요.
Retire on-premises file servers Improve remote work and collaboration Prepare content for Microsoft 365 Copilot Reduce storage and backup complexity Standardize permissions and lifecycle management

File server migration architectureCopy less, govern more 01File server sourceIdentify shares, owners, stale data, sensitive files and business-critical folders. 02Inventory and permission reviewClean duplicate data, inherited permissions, orphaned users and unclear ownership. 03Target platformChoose SharePoint, OneDrive or Azure Files based on collaboration and access needs. 04Information governanceApply lifecycle, permissions, labels, DLP, retention and Copilot readiness controls.

SharePoint and OneDrive provide Microsoft 365 content collaboration. Azure Files provides managed SMB/NFS file shares and has a different access, backup and data-protection model. SPMT migrates supported file shares to Microsoft 365; it is not an Azure Files migration tool. For classic SMB shares, choose the Azure Files migration path for that target, and validate protocol, identity, ACL and metadata support. Do not assume SharePoint retention, container labels or Copilot indexing apply to an Azure file share simply because the files were moved to Azure. Azure Files로 옮길 때 파일 내용과 메타데이터를 나누어 검사하세요. Azure Files FAQ에 따르면 대체 데이터 스트림(ADS)은 Azure 파일 공유에 저장되지 않으며, Azure File Sync를 사용할 때 온프레미스에 남습니다. 또한 대상의 LastAccessTime은 읽기 작업으로 갱신되지 않고 CreationTime과 같습니다. ADS나 최종 접근 시각을 사용하는 업무는 파일 수만 맞는지 확인해서는 이전 성공을 판단할 수 없습니다. Azure Files 메타데이터 지원 범위를 기준으로 시험하세요.

파일 크기 — SharePoint 문서 라이브러리의 업로드 한도는 파일 하나당 250GB입니다. 먼저 한도를 넘는 파일을 찾아 별도 보관할지 결정하세요. 대상 경로 — 대상 폴더 경로와 파일 이름을 합쳐 400자 이내인지 확인하세요. Microsoft의 서비스 설명은 URL을 디코딩한 경로를 기준으로 합니다. 브라우저 주소창에서 복사한 URL 전체 길이로 판정하면 결과가 달라질 수 있습니다. 사용자 PC — 가장 깊은 폴더의 파일을 시험 이관한 뒤, 실제 사용자 PC에서 동기화하고 열기와 이름 변경을 시험하세요. 로컬 동기화 폴더 이름까지 더해지므로 웹에서 열린 파일도 탐색기에서는 경로가 너무 길 수 있습니다. SharePoint 파일 크기·경로 제한 · 플랫폼별 경로 제한과 문제 해결

Inventory shares, size, file types and owners. Identify stale, duplicate and restricted data. Map target locations by business function. Review permissions and external sharing requirements. Run pilot migration and validate access. Execute migration waves with freeze and rollback plan. Decommission legacy shares after acceptance.

Remove orphaned permissions before migration. Avoid copying inherited access blindly. Use sensitivity labels where required. Validate external sharing settings. Keep rollback and read-only archive plans.

Cleanup Which stale, duplicate or restricted content should not migrate? Permissions Which permissions are redesigned instead of copied? Cutover What freeze, rollback and user communication plan is required?

documents.s: Decide what to consolidate, federate or keep separate

documents.t: Global tenant consolidation is not only a migration project. It requires coordinated design across identity, domain, mail coexistence, security policy, compliance policy, data protection, regional administration and user communication. A successful tenant consolidation program should define whether the organization needs full migration, long-term coexistence or a hybrid multi-tenant operating model. Executive lens: Global tenant consolidation is a business operating model decision first and a migration decision second. The key question is which tenants should consolidate, federate, remain isolated or become transitional.

Typical scenarios include: Headquarters and regional subsidiaries using separate Microsoft 365 tenants Acquired companies requiring integration with the parent company Legacy mail systems coexisting with Exchange Online Shared SMTP domain or subdomain routing requirements Regional security and compliance policy differences Data protection and sensitivity label migration requirements Global governance standardization

Area Key Considerations Domain Domain transfer, subdomain routing, DNS, MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC Identity UPN, source identity, target identity, guest access, admin delegation Mail Mail coexistence, forwarding, contacts, mail flow validation Collaboration Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, guest access, external sharing Security Conditional Access, Intune, Defender, download restriction Compliance Purview, sensitivity labels, DLP, retention, audit Administration Administrative Units, regional admin delegation User Impact Sign-in, Outlook, Teams, mobile, communication, hypercare
Target ArchitectureGlobal governance with regional control

Mail coexistence must be designed before domain migration. This is especially important when: Headquarters uses a legacy mail platform Regional subsidiaries use Exchange Online Multiple tenants share similar SMTP domains Users must communicate across mail systems during transition

Mail coexistence patternShared routing without confusing users 01Legacy mail systemKeep primary mailbox service stable while alternate routing addresses are prepared. 02Exchange Online tenantMap Exchange Online recipients, contacts, forwarding and accepted domain behavior. 03Mail routing controlUse alternate SMTP, contacts, connectors or forwarding based on coexistence duration. 04Target recipient experienceTest delivery and replies across each routing path during migration, domain transfer and coexistence.

An Internal relay domain needs the appropriate connector for recipients on the other mail system. See accepted domain types. Element Description Primary SMTP Main user email address Alternate SMTP Routing address for coexistence Mail Contact Object used to route to external or legacy mailbox Forwarding Mail redirection between systems Accepted Domain SMTP domain configured for mail delivery; select Authoritative or Internal relay according to recipient location Connector Mail flow control between systems

When two environments need to share or transition the same SMTP domain, additional routing design is required. One Microsoft 365 tenant owns a custom domain at a time. Cross-tenant synchronization does not let two tenants verify and use the same domain simultaneously. Distinguish legacy-system shared-namespace routing from a domain transfer between Microsoft 365 tenants; use approved alternate routing domains during coexistence. See domain ownership and Outlook cutover behavior.

Option Description Subdomain Routing Use subdomains such as m365.company.com or notes.company.com Alternate Address Assign additional routing addresses per user Mail Contact Routing Create contacts to route messages to the other system Forwarding-Based Coexistence Configure forwarding from source mailbox to target mailbox Full Domain Cutover Remove domain from source and add to target tenant
Domain transfer is a high-impact activity.

Area Impact User Sign-in UPN and login address may change Mail Flow Inbound and outbound mail routing may change Teams Tenant identity and collaboration may be affected Guest Access Existing guest invitations may need to be recreated Mobile Mail profiles may need reconfiguration Outlook Outlook profile may need recreation or reconnection

Lower DNS TTL before cutover Freeze domain and proxy address changes Validate all users, aliases and contacts Prepare domain removal checklist Prepare rollback plan Validate mail flow immediately after cutover
Headquarters uses a legacy mail platform while regional users use Exchange Online.

Requirement Recommendation Mail delivery between systems Configure alternate SMTP routing Legacy user visibility in M365 Create mail contacts or mail users Exchange Online user visibility in legacy mail Create equivalent routing objects Migration wave support Use forwarding and staged validation Cutover readiness Validate mail flow both directions
After tenant consolidation, users may no longer use the original regional tenant identity.
Guest access to external tenants Teams membership Shared channels External collaboration Application access MFA registration Conditional Access policy scope
Create an identity transition plan that includes: Source identity mapping Target identity assignment Guest re-invitation plan MFA re-registration guidance Application access validation

For native migration, Microsoft Migration Orchestrator supports mailboxes, OneDrive, Teams chats and meetings. It does not move identities or all Teams and SharePoint content. See the workload support summary before selecting tools. Tenant consolidation can affect Teams collaboration.

Area Consideration Teams Membership Membership must be validated after migration Chat History Migration capability depends on tooling Private Channels Requires special validation Shared Channels Cross-tenant collaboration must be reviewed Meeting Links Existing links may need communication Guest Users Guests may need to be re-invited
Sensitivity labels and protected documents require special planning.

Existing labels may be tenant-specific Encrypted documents may not be readable after migration without proper handling Label policies must be recreated or mapped in the target tenant Protected files may require decryption or relabeling before migration DLP and retention policies must be reviewed in the target tenant For native SharePoint cross-tenant moves, sites containing files with user-defined-permission sensitivity labels cannot move until those labels are removed. Plan any protection changes with the data owner and reapply the approved target protection. See the SharePoint migration prerequisites and label restrictions.

Step Activity 1 Inventory sensitivity labels and protected content 2 Identify encrypted or restricted documents 3 Define label mapping between source and target tenant 4 Validate sample document access after migration 5 Reapply target tenant label policy 6 Validate user access and compliance controls
A single Microsoft 365 tenant can support regional policy differences. However, policy separation should generally be designed by group, not by domain alone.

These are scoping options to assess, not interchangeable settings. Check the supported assignment type and exclusions for each product and policy. Policy Area Separation Method Conditional Access User or group assignment Intune User group or device group Sensitivity Label Policy User or group targeting DLP Policy scope and conditions Defender Device group or user scope SharePoint Access Site, group and CA policy
Administrative Units can provide limited regional administration.
Regional password reset Regional user management Limited help desk delegation Regional device support Location-based administrative scope

Administrative Units do not provide complete tenant-level separation. They are suitable for delegated administration but not for full regional autonomy. Administrative units scope supported Entra management permissions; they do not hide all other directory objects or delegate Intune device management. Use Intune RBAC and scope tags for that separate workload. See supported administrative unit scenarios.

For SharePoint and OneDrive content, Conditional Access and configured SharePoint unmanaged-device controls can provide limited web access. The result depends on policy scope, device state and supported clients; being a guest or an employee does not set it automatically. Other workloads require their own access design. See unmanaged-device access controls.

A global tenant consolidation engagement should produce: Current Tenant Landscape Domain and Mail Coexistence Design Identity Mapping Plan Security Policy Mapping Purview and Sensitivity Label Review Regional Policy Design Administrative Unit Design Migration or Coexistence Roadmap Cutover Runbook User Communication Plan Hypercare Plan

Do not start with migration tooling. Start with the operating model decision. The organization should first decide whether the target state is: One tenant with unified governance Multiple tenants with cross-tenant collaboration Hybrid coexistence with phased migration Only after this decision should the technical migration approach be finalized.

documents.t: A Google Workspace migration program covers supported mail, calendar, contacts and Drive content, plus the redesign of collaboration workflows for Microsoft 365. The program should be planned as identity, data, collaboration and change management workstreams. A mail-only view misses user behavior, file ownership and coexistence complexity.
Google Workspace의 메일·일정·연락처와 Drive 자료를 Microsoft 365로 옮길 때 필요한 준비 사항입니다. 계정과 도메인, 별칭·그룹, 파일 소유권과 외부 공유를 점검하세요. Exchange의 메일 이전과 Drive 자료 이전은 도구와 지원 범위를 따로 확인합니다.

Consolidate collaboration platforms Move from Gmail and Drive to Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive Standardize identity and security controls Prepare Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption Reduce duplicate licensing and administration

Google Workspace migration pathIdentity, data, collaboration, adoption 01Google WorkspaceInventory Gmail, Calendar, Drive, shared drives, groups, aliases and external collaborators. 02AssessmentMap identity, domain, mail, calendar, Drive ownership and coexistence complexity. 03Microsoft 365 targetMove to Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and security baseline. 04User adoptionSupport behavior change, training, migration waves and post-cutover hypercare.

Assess users, aliases, groups, mail routing and Drive ownership. Design identity and coexistence model. Prepare Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams. Run pilot migration for representative users. Plan communication, training and support. Execute migration waves. Validate mail flow, calendars, permissions and file access.

Use Exchange Online's documented Google Workspace mailbox migration for mail, calendar and contacts. For Google Drive files, use Migration Manager for Google Workspace, not SharePoint Migration Tool (SPMT): SPMT supports on-premises SharePoint and file shares as sources. Review Google Drive identity mapping and permission settings separately; mapping a user alone does not enable file-level permission migration. See Migration Manager's current workflow.

Exchange의 Google Workspace 배치 이전은 개인 일정과 회의실 예약을 별개로 처리합니다. 회의실 예약과 공유 캘린더는 이전 대상에서 빠집니다. Microsoft의 이전 항목과 제한 시험 이전 전에 회의실을 예약한 일정 하나와 반복 일정 하나를 고릅니다. 주최자, 회의실, 날짜와 시간을 기록합니다. 이전 후 주최자의 Outlook 일정과 대상 회의실 캘린더를 각각 엽니다. 참석자 추적 화면에 수락으로 표시돼도 회의실 캘린더에서 같은 시간에 예약을 찾을 수 있는지 확인합니다. 반복 일정은 다음 회차도 확인합니다. 예약이 빠졌다면 기존 예약과 겹치는지 확인한 뒤 주최자가 대상 회의실로 요청을 보냅니다. 회의실 캘린더에 예약이 생기면 점검을 마칩니다. 메일 규칙은 이전 후 기본적으로 꺼져 있습니다. 사용자가 Outlook에서 규칙의 조건과 이동 대상 폴더를 확인한 뒤 필요한 규칙만 켜세요. 메일 이전 전에 대상 사용자를 메일 사용 가능 사용자(mail-enabled user)로 준비하고, 배치마다 이전할 사용자 목록을 지정해야 합니다. 이 Exchange 이전 경로는 GCC High·DoD에서 제공되지 않습니다. 일정 색상과 부재중·자동 회신 설정은 이전되지 않으며, 연락처당 이메일 주소는 최대 3개까지만 이전됩니다. 메일 이전의 준비 사항과 제한을 시험 목록에 반영하세요. Drive의 파일별 권한과 이전 버전은 별도 이전 설정을 확인해야 합니다. 계정 매핑이 끝났다는 이유만으로 파일 권한과 모든 버전이 함께 복사된다고 판단하지 마세요. Migration Manager 준비 사항에 따라 대상 경로·권한·버전 설정을 각각 확인합니다.

Review third-party app access before migration. Map Google groups to Microsoft 365 groups carefully. Validate sharing links and external collaborators. Apply Conditional Access and device compliance after migration readiness.

This Migration section provides enterprise migration guidance for Microsoft 365, Exchange Online, Google Workspace, file server, SharePoint, Teams and tenant scenarios. A tenant-to-tenant migration program coordinates account preparation, supported content moves and the recreation or reconfiguration of target governance controls. The migration tool does not automatically transfer every identity, policy or workload. Typical business drivers include: Merger & Acquisition Divestiture Global IT Consolidation Regulatory Separation Tenant Rationalization Unlike simple mailbox migrations, Tenant-to-Tenant projects impact identity, collaboration, security, compliance and end-user productivity. The objective is to minimize business disruption while preserving data integrity, permissions and governance. Microsoft Migration Orchestrator coordinates Exchange mailboxes, OneDrive, Teams chats and Teams meetings. It moves content, not identities; prepare identity mapping and the required user configuration separately. Teams meetings require both chats and mailbox migration in the batch. SharePoint sites, Teams channels, apps and device policies need separate migration plans. Check the per-user Cross Tenant User Data Migration add-on and workload exclusions in the orchestrator documentation. Identity Mapping requires a mailbox in the source tenant and a MailUser without a mailbox in the target tenant, even when the batch does not move mailboxes. For OneDrive, the native orchestrator moves content and leaves a redirect; it does not support incremental or delta migration passes. CompleteAfterDate starts the remaining workloads after Exchange cutover rather than guaranteeing that every workload is complete at that time. Plan the user outage around these dependencies; migration completion is not covered by an SLA. Microsoft Native Quest BitTitan AvePoint Fly

For the native orchestrator's Teams chats and meetings, source content remains, potentially with changed participant lists or duplicate threads in either tenant. After migration, users should work with their target identity. Access to out-of-scope source content still requires a licensed source user, so do not remove source access merely because mailbox migration has finished. See Teams chat and meeting scope.
